
❯ Write a 100-word poem about wind, no tools.

● Wind has no face, only evidence:
  the wheat bowing in long green waves,
  a gate that argues with its latch,
  laundry rehearsing flight on the line.
  It carries the smell of distant rain,
  the gossip of chimneys, a stranger's song.
  It combs the dunes and rearranges them,
  patient as a clerk with endless time.
  At night it tries every door,
  whistles through the keyhole,
  asks the old house what it remembers.
  I have stood on the hill, arms wide,
  and felt it lean against me like a friend
  who cannot stay, who never says goodbye,
  only moves on, still singing.

✻ Churned for 14s · done 4:46 AM

❯ Write a 100-word poem about fire, no tools.

● Fire begins as a small persuasion,
  a match's brief argument with the dark.
